annotation.title_clean: From an Eco-Relational Approach to Ecologically Responsible Robot Ethics
annotation.title_en: From an Eco-Relational Approach to Ecologically Responsible Robot Ethics
annotation.summary_en: Reply commentary in Philosophy & Technology responding to Gellers' critique of the author's eco-relational approach in robot ethics. It defends the method and argues that robot ethics must incorporate relations with non-human entities and be ecologically responsible, bridging philosophical relational approaches with applied ethics and law.
key_provisions_or_claims: Autonomy, agency and responsibility must include relations with non-human entities from the start.
Defends focusing on ethical concepts rather than imposing specific ethical systems.
Supports Gellers' call for an ecologically-sensitive ethical orientation in robot ethics.
Argues relational approaches should be connected to applied ethics and law, not separated.
Calls for more non-Western perspectives such as Ubuntu and techno-animism in robot ethics.
